title: Fibre products distribute over a finite coproduct
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $(u_i:U_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ be a finite family of morphisms of schemes, and put $V=\coprod_{i\in I}U_i$ with its induced morphism to $X$. For every integer $p\ge0$, there is a canonical isomorphism of schemes over $X$ $$V\times_X\cdots\times_XV\;\cong\;\coprod_{(i_0,\ldots,i_p)\in I^{p+1}} U_{i_0}\times_X\cdots\times_XU_{i_p},$$ with $p+1$ factors on the left. Under this isomorphism, every projection omitting a factor restricts on the summand indexed by $(i_0,\ldots,i_p)$ to the corresponding projection between the indexed fibre products.

source.place: Schemes, Lemmas Tags 01JB and 01JC (lemma-glue and lemma-glue-schemes), applied to the disjoint coproduct pieces, together with the universal property of fibre products in Section 26.17

proof.text: Write $\iota_i:U_i\to V$ for the coprojections of [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family], and for $p\ge0$ let $V^{p+1}=V\times_X\cdots\times_XV$ and $U_J=U_{j_0}\times_X\cdots\times_XU_{j_p}$ for $J=(j_0,\ldots,j_p)\in I^{p+1}$, the iterated fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product] being formed from the left, $V^{p+2}=V^{p+1}\times_XV$ and $U_{(J,i)}=U_J\times_XU_i$. Let $\varphi_J:U_J\to V^{p+1}$ be the morphism $\iota_{j_0}\times_X\cdots\times_X\iota_{j_p}$, i.e. the unique morphism whose $r$-th projection is $\iota_{j_r}$ composed with the $r$-th projection of $U_J$; it is a morphism over $X$ since $u\circ\iota_{j_r}=u_{j_r}$. By the universal property of the coproduct [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] the $\varphi_J$ glue to a unique morphism $\varphi_p:\coprod_{J\in I^{p+1}}U_J\to V^{p+1}$ over $X$ with $\varphi_p$ restricted to the summand $J$ equal to $\varphi_J$.

source.place: Schemes, Section 26.17 (universal property of fibre products), with the coproduct of schemes of Tags 01JB and 01JC (lemma-glue, lemma-glue-schemes)

proof.text: We prove by induction on $p\ge0$ that $\varphi_p$ is an isomorphism. For $p=0$, $\varphi_0$ is the morphism $\coprod_iU_i\to V$ with $\varphi_0\circ\iota_i=\iota_i$ for every $i$, so $\varphi_0=\mathrm{id}_V$ by the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family].

source.place: Schemes, Tags 01JB and 01JC (lemma-glue, lemma-glue-schemes): base of the induction

proof.text: Inductive step: assume $\varphi_p$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-sc-etale-fibre-product-base-change-coproduct] applied to the family $(U_i\to X)_{i\in I}$ and $T=V^{p+1}$, the morphism $\alpha:\coprod_{i\in I}V^{p+1}\times_XU_i\to V^{p+1}\times_XV=V^{p+2}$ which is $\mathrm{id}\times_X\iota_i$ on the summand $i$ is an isomorphism. For each $i$, $\varphi_p$ is an isomorphism over $X$ from the coproduct $\coprod_JU_J$ (with its induced morphism to $X$) to $V^{p+1}$, so $\varphi_p\times_X\mathrm{id}_{U_i}$ is an isomorphism (functoriality in [def-pc-fibre-product], applied to $\varphi_p$ and its inverse); and [lem-sc-etale-fibre-product-base-change-coproduct] applied to the family $(U_J\to X)_{J\in I^{p+1}}$ and $T=U_i$, followed on both sides by the exchange of the two factors (an isomorphism by the uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product]), shows that the morphism $\beta_i:\coprod_JU_J\times_XU_i\to(\coprod_JU_J)\times_XU_i$ which is $\iota_J\times_X\mathrm{id}_{U_i}$ on the summand $J$ is an isomorphism. Hence $\alpha\circ\coprod_i((\varphi_p\times_X\mathrm{id}_{U_i})\circ\beta_i)$ is an isomorphism from $\coprod_i\coprod_JU_{(J,i)}=\coprod_{(J,i)\in I^{p+2}}U_{(J,i)}$ (a coproduct of coproducts is the coproduct over the union of the index sets, by the universal property in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]) to $V^{p+2}$. On the summand $(J,i)$ it is $(\varphi_J\times_X\mathrm{id}_{U_i})$ followed by $\mathrm{id}\times_X\iota_i$, i.e. $\varphi_J\times_X\iota_i=\varphi_{(J,i)}$: both have the same projections to $V^{p+1}$ and to $V$, so they agree by the uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product]. By the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] this isomorphism is $\varphi_{p+1}$, which completes the induction. So for every $p\ge0$, $\varphi_p$ is an isomorphism of schemes over $X$, the canonical isomorphism of the statement.

source.place: Schemes, Tags 01JB and 01JC (lemma-glue, lemma-glue-schemes) and Section 26.17, applied inductively after base change

proof.text: Let $\pi:V^{p+1}\to V^{p}$ be a projection omitting the $r$-th factor ($p\ge1$), and $\pi_J:U_J\to U_{J'}$ the corresponding projection, $J'$ being $J$ with $j_r$ omitted. Then $\pi\circ\varphi_J$ and $\varphi_{J'}\circ\pi_J$ have the same projections to each remaining factor $V$, namely $\iota_{j_s}$ composed with the $s$-th projection of $U_J$ ($s\ne r$), so they are equal by the uniqueness in [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus under the isomorphism $\varphi_p$ of Step 3, $\pi$ restricts on the summand $J$ to $\pi_J$ followed by the coprojection of the summand $J'$.

lean.statement: theorem etale_fibre_product_coproduct (X : Scheme.{u}) (I : Type v) [Finite I] (U : I → Scheme.{u}) (u : ∀ i : I, U i ⟶ X) : let A : I → Over X := fun i => Over.mk (u i) let V : Over X := Over.mk (Sigma.desc u) let P := fun (p : ℕ) (J : Fin (p + 1) → I) => ∏ᶜ fun r => A (J r) let Q := fun p : ℕ => ∏ᶜ fun _ : Fin (p + 1) => V let c : ∀ i : I, A i ⟶ V := fun i => Over.homMk (Sigma.ι U i) (Sigma.ι_desc u i) ∃ e : ∀ p : ℕ, (∐ P p) ≅ Q p, (∀ (p : ℕ) (J : Fin (p + 1) → I) (r : Fin (p + 1)), Sigma.ι (P p) J ≫ (e p).hom ≫ Pi.π (fun _ : Fin (p + 1) => V) r = Pi.π (fun s : Fin (p + 1) => A (J s)) r ≫ c (J r)) ∧ (∀ (p : ℕ) (J : Fin (p + 2) → I) (r : Fin (p + 2)), Sigma.ι (P (p + 1)) J ≫ (e (p + 1)).hom ≫ Pi.lift (fun s : Fin (p + 1) => Pi.π (fun _ : Fin (p + 2) => V) (r.succAbove s)) = Pi.lift (fun s : Fin (p + 1) => Pi.π (fun t : Fin (p + 2) => A (J t)) (r.succAbove s)) ≫ Sigma.ι (P p) (fun s => J (r.succAbove s)) ≫ (e p).hom)
